title: Cap. III Sol. Rat. 3: efficacious end-intention before victory; God more than agonothetes
pass_a_gloss: Second, what Vasquez assumes, that a Prince cannot efficaciously intend that someone obtain the prize except from a foreseen intuition of merits, is not of so explored a truth as he opines. For there is an efficacious intention of the end which moves the agent to apply efficaciously whatsoever means he can to the obtaining of the same: although it be not in his power certainly to foresee the event, or infallibly to obtain the end itself. A Prince therefore from special benevolence can seriously and efficaciously intend the prize for his friend before the intuition of victory; and from this intention not only wish, but as far as in him is, prepare and give him all things that conduce to victory; although as judge and agonothetes he cannot actually crown him except upon intuition of the victory obtained. God therefore much more (for whom to will and to do are equally at hand) can efficaciously intend for Peter or Paul the crown of eternal glory, and from the force of this intention prepare and give them all those things which are called merits of the crown; and in this his predestination from eternity foresee their merits, and at length upon intuition of the fight nobly fought place the destined crown upon their heads.
pass_b_english: Second, Vasquez’s claim that a prince cannot efficaciously intend someone’s prize except from foresight of merits is not as settled as he thinks. Efficacious intention of an end moves the agent to apply every means in his power toward obtaining it — even when he cannot certainly foresee the event or infallibly secure the end. So a prince from special goodwill can seriously and efficaciously intend the prize for his friend before seeing the victory, and from that intention not only wish but, as far as he can, prepare and give all that helps toward victory — though as judge and agonothetes he cannot actually crown him except upon the victory won. God much more (for whom to will and to do are ready alike) can efficaciously intend for Peter or Paul the crown of eternal glory, and by that intention’s force prepare and give all that are called merits of the crown; and in this predestination from eternity foresee their merits, and at last, upon the fight nobly fought, set the destined crown on their heads.
source_text: Secundo, quod assumit Vasques, non posse Principem intendere efficaciter ut aliquis consequatur premium, nisi ex praeviso intuitu meritorum, non est tam exploratae veritatis, atque ille opinatur. Est enim efficax intentio finis, quae movet agentem ut efficaciter adhibeat quaecunque potest media ad eiusdem consecutionem: licet non sit in eius potestate certo praevidere eventum, aut infallibiliter ipsum finem consequi. Potest igitur Princeps ex speciali benevolentia serio & efficaciter intendere praemium amico suo ante intuitum victoriae; atque ex hac intentione non modo optare, sed quantum in illo est, parare & dare illi omnia quae conducunt ad victoriam; quamvis ut judex & agonothetes non possit illum actu coronare, nisi intuitu victoriae obtentae. Deus ergo multo magis (cui velle & facere aeque in promptu sunt) potest efficaciter intendere Petro aut Paulo coronam aeternae gloriae, atque ex vi hujus intentionis praeparate & dare illis ea omnia quae merita coronae dicuntur; atque in hac sua praedestinatione ab aeterno praevidere illorum merita, atque tandem intuitu pugnae praeclare depugnatae coronam destinatam illorum capitibus imponere.
